messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — after enabling activation checkpointing across the TP/PP stack I see a 18-25% throughput drop and larger all-reduce latency variance. Profiling attached below, need quick triage.
priya: Can you paste the profiler output? which workload (length / beams / batch_tokens)?
jordan: workload was gen: batch=16, max_len=2048, decode greedy, kv-cache warmed per prefix.
alex: pasted perf dump: ```
# baseline (no checkpoint)
step=100 kernel_allreduce=120ms compute=200ms comm=140ms overlap=30ms total_step=420ms
# with activation checkpointing enabled
step=100 kernel_allreduce=210ms compute=300ms comm=260ms overlap=20ms total_step=650ms
# note: comm increased a lot, overlap decreased
```
priya: hmm that suggests recompute is increasing per-stage compute which shifts the compute/comm balance and kills overlap. Are we seeing extra NCCL launches (small allreduces) vs fewer big ones?
nick: I captured nvprof traces — looks like TP micro-batches are producing more frequent smaller all-reduces (lots of 32-64KB ops) after recompute because layers are re-evaluated and trigger KV flush patterns.
samantha: small allreduces are expensive due to latency overhead and NCCL kernel selection falls back to algorithm with worse perf for tiny payloads. We should try aggregating the all-reduces (delay reduce) or switch to async NN for small messages.
priya: Also KV-cache behavior: with recompute we recompute keys/values rather than reuse cached ones for some micro-batches, leading to repeated KV inserts and extra inter-node chatter. That explains extra comm.
jordan: Repro script I ran: ```bash
PYTORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=INFO python -m torch.distributed.launch --nproc_per_node=4 run_eval.py --batch 16 --max-len 2048 --checkpoint=activation
```
alex: Proposed mitigations: 1) change kernel selection policy in runtime to prefer tree-based allreduce for <128KB payloads, 2) add micro-batch aggregation window to delay small reduces, 3) adapt batching heuristic: reduce recompute frequency for short-prefix KV-heavy requests, 4) add KV prefetch/pinned-populate to avoid re-insert churn.
priya: For 1) we can add a perf table mapping payload size -> ncclAlgorithm and force tune in the runtime. We did similar for matmul kernels.
nick: For 2) I sketched an aggregator: hold up to X micro-batches or Y ms before issuing reduce, then emit a single fused all-reduce. Risk: latency tail increases for small latency-sensitive requests. We can make it policy-driven per route.
samantha: For 3) heuristic idea: if seq_prefix_len < threshold and kv_hit_rate high, skip checkpoint for first N layers (cheap remat) to preserve overlap. This is coarse but could recover overlap cheaply.
jordan: I ran quick patch to prefer NCCL_TREE for <256KB and saw kernel_allreduce drop from 210ms -> 150ms in the checkpoint case, overall step -> 540ms (not full recovery but notable).
perf-bot: perf-regression-alert: thread=1769991110 metric=throughput drop=22% trigger=activation-checkpointing-flag. Added tag: regression/pp-tp/comm-overlap.
alex: Good. Action items: @priya evaluate kernel selection table + run full sweep on V100/A100/H100; @nick prototype aggregator with 5ms window; @samantha prototype heuristic to skip remat for first 4 layers when prefix_len < 128; @jordan run end-to-end eval on ded. Also create a follow-up perf job for mixed-batch sizes.
priya: I'll start with device matrix and post CSV. If NCCL tuning helps we can make it opt-in per deployment.
nick: I'll test aggregator on a 4xA100 dev pool and report perf/latency percentiles.
samantha: I'll open a short doc describing the remat-skip heuristic and expected correctness tradeoffs.
jordan: one more note — KV sharding across PP boundaries currently assumes single populate ordering; recompute causes duplicate population attempts which serialize due to a small spinlock we have. That spinlock needs to become compare-and-insert to avoid serializing.
alex: Good catch. Add that to infra/low-level tasks. Anyone want to own the ticket?
samantha: I'll file it and tag eng-runtime + eng-ml, ticket RLW-1742.
perf-bot: summary: immediate wins = kernel hint table + reduce aggregation; medium = remat-skip heuristic + KV insert refactor; long = smarter per-route policies.
alex: Thanks all — let's reconvene after the first experiments. :thumbsup:
